name: Paper trading btc-regime-trend on ETH and SOL

sections.hypothesis: btc-regime-trend on ETH and SOL, traded forward through Kestrel on Binance's Spot Testnet, (a) behaves exactly as the backtest model says it should, and (b) keeps beating each coin held at the same average exposure on data that didn't exist when it was designed.
sections.rationale: On pursue since 2026-11-16 (Claude's call, delegated by Luke): found by searching other altcoins and confirmed once on 180 unsearched ones (83% of coins, 55% of walk-forward windows); on ETH and SOL it passes every scorecard test but luck (Sharpe 1.33 and 1.72, walk-forward 4 of 7 and 4 of 6, robust). Both coins' holdout years were spent by trend-vol-target, so forward data is the only fresh test. Minimum track record from its backtest daily returns (Bailey and Lopez de Prado): 320 days (ETH) and 176 days (SOL) for 90% confidence that the true Sharpe is above zero (527 and 289 for 95%); it runs 395 days, matching the trend-vol-target accounts, so all paper accounts are reviewed together. It leans on BTC's trend as trend-vol-target does, so running both on the same coins side by side shows whether it adds anything. Each coin is its own account with its own 330 USDT. The testnet proves the plumbing; its prices come from the test order book, so the strategy is judged on the model replay at real Binance prices, which makes the same decisions by construction.
sections.rules: Two accounts: kestrel paper open brt-eth --symbol ETHUSDT --strategy btc-regime-trend --research <this note> --venue testnet --cash 330, and the same for brt-sol on SOLUSDT; then kestrel paper schedule for each (hourly at 10 past; idempotent). Default settings (BTC above its 50-day average, the coin up over 30 days, sized to 50% volatility over 30 days), daily bars, the [risk] limits in kestrel.toml. Each run refreshes BTCUSDT for btc_close and refuses to decide a bar with a missing input. The accounts share the testnet login with tvt-eth and tvt-sol: each keeps its own ledger, and reconciliation requires the exchange to hold at least what each ledger says. Runs 395 days from its first decision. Reviewed every 3 months with kestrel paper track and the Trading page. Interim reviews report; only the 6-month check can end it, and only for failure (no stopping early on a good run).
sections.falsification: Plumbing, at every review: any decision that differs from the model is a bug, fixed before the test continues (not a strategy failure); missed days must stay under 5% of days handled; a refusal for a missing input is a plumbing event to investigate. Early failure, at 182 days only: if a coin's model replay is behind that coin held at its average exposure on both Sharpe and return, Claude recommends stopping that coin and Luke decides. Strategy, at 395 days, each coin separately: the model replay must (1) have a probabilistic Sharpe of at least 90%, (2) beat the coin held at its average exposure over the whole period, by Sharpe if holding's Sharpe is positive and by return if it isn't, and (3) keep its worst drawdown no deeper than 50%. Failing any one means Claude recommends drop and Luke decides. Reported beside trend-vol-target on the same coin over the same days, deciding nothing. A safety halt pauses the test for Luke to decide; it isn't resumed without a recorded reason.
sections.parameters: btc_days 50, coin_days 30, vol_days 30, target_vol_pct 50 (the defaults; never changed during the test).
sections.costs: Modelled at kestrel.toml's costs (7.5 bps fees with the BNB discount, plus each coin's spread). Until the venue handles BNB fees, testnet fills pay 10 bps, so tracking will show fees slightly above the model. Paper trading is not a trial: nothing is chosen from it.

history.reason: Accounts brt-eth and brt-sol opened on the testnet 2026-11-16; first decision the 2026-11-15 bar.
